1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money, they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 of them are open source.

Here's what surprised me most. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. One in seven. Think about how many hours you've burned staring at a red build that was never a real failure.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

But failure is part of success, not the opposite of it.

The reason they left? They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we listened, we learned, and we built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. It changed how we think about our customers, not just our product.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson is that your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough.

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build. You just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

We built an app we were proud of. Almost nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we figured restaurant staff would love our sleek mobile app. They didn't. In the first month, only 12% of staff even opened it.

That stung. Then it clicked. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025, we made the call and moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets use it now, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

Hardware is hard. Here is our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise did not go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. That is not who we are.

We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We did not stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we have had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes do not define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

Now our 4 vets do around 30 home visits a week. Each one reminds me why we left the clinic.

Your pet stays calm. You stay calm. The medicine gets better.

Following your heart isn't soft. Sometimes it's the bravest call you'll make.
